methodological_rigor.justification: Observational cohort with clear CNB diagnostic protocol applied by experienced operators (13 and 25 years experience) across 286 patients with 316 nodules. Appropriate statistical methods include chi-square/Fisher's exact tests, logistic regression for risk factors, and calculation of sensitivity/specificity. Limitations acknowledged: single-center design, selection bias from enriched cohort, univariate analysis only due to limited inconclusive events.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Individual cohort study (LoE 2b) with direct clinical relevance to thyroid nodule diagnosis. Demonstrates practical utility of CNB as first-line diagnostic tool for selected nodules with suspicious imaging features. Results inform clinical decision-making regarding alternative to FNA, though acknowledged as complementary rather than replacement strategy.

reporting_quality.justification: Observational study with structured reporting of methods, results including diagnostic categories, and comprehensive discussion of limitations. STROBE principles evident (patient selection criteria, data collection, statistical analysis) though not explicitly cited. No mention of data sharing, code availability, or deposition in repositories; protocols appear irreproducible without direct contact.

novelty_literature.justification: Meaningful extension of prior work on CNB as first-line diagnostic tool. Real-world evaluation in 2022-2023 with 316 nodules adds empirical data to support CNB effectiveness, but concept not new; meta-analysis cited (Chung et al. 2018) with similar findings. Contribution is confirmatory and pragmatic rather than mechanistically novel.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear introduction establishing clinical problem, structured methods with detailed technical descriptions and diagnostic categories, comprehensive results with subgroup analyses, and thorough discussion addressing limitations and contextualizing findings against prior literature. Minor issue: some categorical definitions could be more concise, but overall publication-ready.

key_strengths: Large real-world cohort (316 nodules) with diagnostic categorization using established Korean Endocrine Pathology framework
Experienced operators (13 and 25 years) performing all CNB procedures, minimizing technique variability
Comprehensive comparison with alternative diagnostic modalities (FNA, CEUS, surgical confirmation) and explicit discussion of selection bias
Subgroup analysis by nodule size revealing differential diagnostic performance; no hemorrhage or needle tract seeding complications
Thorough limitation discussion including verification bias mitigation and acknowledgment that results may not generalize to routine screening
key_concerns: Single-center study with enriched cohort (higher malignancy prevalence) limiting generalizability to unselected thyroid nodules in routine clinical practice

Benign diagnoses in 70 of 78 benign nodules (89.7%) established using non-surgical reference standards (CEUS, follow-up stability), introducing verification bias and potentially inflating specificity/NPV estimates
Univariate logistic regression only for inconclusive outcomes due to small sample; wide confidence intervals reported for estimates reaching 100% (e.g., sensitivity in <1 cm nodules)
Subset of 39 undiagnosed lesions (12.3% of cohort) excluded from analysis; malignant potential of Category III/IV/V lesions managed conservatively without definitive confirmation
No data sharing statement or code availability; methods not fully reproducible without institutional protocols
chief_reviewer.rationale: Competent, well-reported observational study with solid methodological rigor but not practice-changing. Appropriate for Tier 3 (4-9.9 JIF) due to incremental confirmation of CNB utility in real-world setting. Minor revisions could strengthen claims and clarify undiagnosed cohort management.
